articles.title: Global Artists Bring Theatre, Music and Magic to Karachi on Seventh Day of World Culture Festival
articles.description: From Norwegian detective theatre for children to French Sufi-inspired music, the seventh day of the third World Culture Festival 2026 brought an eclectic mix of international performances, workshops and films to Karachi.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, UrduPoint / APP, November 4-5, 2026
articles.body:
From Norwegian detective theatre for children to French Sufi-inspired music, the seventh day of the third World Culture Festival 2026 brought an eclectic mix of international performances, workshops and films to Karachi, as artists from Norway, Italy, France and the United States explored diverse forms of artistic expression at the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi, The Express Tribune reported on November 5.

Theatre and workshops through the day

The day's programme opened with Gangster Hunting With Daisy Detective, a children's theatre production by Norway's Erler Teaterkompani. Renowned Italian theatre artist Tom Corradini conducted a special workshop on physical comedy and clowning, attracting a large number of young actors, artists and members of the public. French artist Zakaria Haffar conducted a musical workshop titled Vocal, during which participants learned about vocal techniques, musical notes and rhythm. The festival also presented The Interview, a theatre production by American artist Gillian Rhodes.

Films from Türkiye and France

The film screening programme featured four films from Türkiye and France: Aboveground-Underground, Platform 1, About My Mom and La Petite École, exploring family, social and migrant-life themes, according to UrduPoint. The day's programme concluded with a captivating musical performance titled SAMA: UN AUTRE SOUFFLE by French artist Joanna Senem Goodale, described as a soulful fusion of classical piano and Pakistani classical music.

A 25-day festival

The third World Culture Festival Karachi 2026 runs from October 29 to November 22, 2026, organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi with the support of the Sindh Government. The festival features approximately 1,000 international artists from more than 150 countries, alongside over 500 Pakistani artists, presenting theatre, music, dance, films, visual arts and traditional cultural performances. The public can attend through free registration, and the festival continues at the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi until November 22.

articles.title: Saba Qamar Teases Case No. 10 as Shooting Begins, With Tabish Hashmi Making His TV Acting Debut
articles.description: Shooting for Case No. 10 has officially begun in November 2026, Saba Qamar shared on Instagram, with the Shahzeb Khanzada-written drama directed by Danish Nawaz and Tabish Hashmi joining the cast.
articles.body:
Shooting for Case No. 10 has officially begun in November 2026, as actress Saba Qamar shared photos on Instagram, The Current reported on November 5. She wrote, “Some very special cases are coming together for Case No. 10.”

Who is behind the project

Geo News anchor Shahzeb Khanzada has written the drama, while Danish Nawaz directs it and Badar Mehmood produces it. Tabish Hashmi is joining the cast, making his television acting debut. Saba Qamar also shared behind-the-scenes glimpses from a script reading session for the project, with pictures featuring her alongside co-star Tabish Hashmi, writer Shahzeb Khanzada and director Danish Nawaz, 24NewsHD reported. Further details about the storyline, cast and release date have not yet been shared, the reports noted.

What the story is reported to be about

Reports said the story revolves around a murder mystery or a high-profile drug case in Pakistan, while 24NewsHD described the project as a biopic based on the story of Pinky, who has been described as a drug dealer. Those descriptions come from early reports and the project's own social media posts, and the production has not yet confirmed a full synopsis, so the exact shape of the story remains to be seen.

A strong year for Saba Qamar

Saba Qamar earned wide praise for three hit dramas this year: Pamaal, Case No. 9, and Muamma. In Case No. 9 she played Seher Muazzam, a rape survivor who fights back courageously and ultimately secures justice. The new project continues her run of courtroom and crime-adjacent drama, and with a journalist-turned-writer, a proven director and a popular host making his acting debut, Case No. 10 already carries more attention than most dramas manage before a single episode airs. Viewers will now watch for a teaser and a broadcast date.

articles.title: Children's Theatre Takes Centre Stage on Day Six of World Culture Festival Karachi
articles.description: The sixth day of the 3rd World Culture Festival Karachi 2026 featured two children's theatre productions, Polish short films, music and dance, and the Urdu-English play 'English Only'.
articles.body:
The sixth day of the 25-day 3rd World Culture Festival Karachi 2026, organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi, featured two children's theatre productions, music, film screenings, dance and the Urdu-English theatre play English Only, The Express Tribune reported on November 4.

The children's programme

The programme for children opened with Little Red Riding Hood, presented by Poland's Miniatura City Theatre. Norwegian theatre group Erler Teaterkompani presented the adventure-filled production Gangster Hunting with Daisy Detective. Under the film screening segment, Polish Featurette presented four short films from Poland: Blue Bird, Momo & Lulu, Dream Up the Title and The Town That Drove Away.

The evening show

At 7 p.m., the Urdu-English theatre production English Only, directed by Awab Bin Farhat, was staged. The festival, which runs through November 22 at the Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi, brings together over 1,000 international artists from 150-plus countries alongside 500 Pakistani performers, with daily programming across theatre, music, dance and visual arts and public access via complimentary registration, earlier festival coverage reported.

articles.title: Kinza Hashmi Reported for Shakib Khan's 'Mohabbat' — but the Casting Is Not Yet Confirmed
articles.description: Pakistani actress Kinza Hashmi is reportedly set to make her Bangladeshi film debut opposite Shakib Khan in 'Mohabbat', sources close to the production say — though the director and producer have yet to confirm the casting publicly.
articles.body:
Pakistani actress and model Kinza Hashmi is reportedly set to make her Bangladeshi film debut opposite Shakib Khan in his upcoming film ‘Mohabbat’, according to sources close to the production cited by TOB News on November 4 — a report, not a confirmed announcement.

What is reported — and what is not

Several sources close to the production have indicated that Kinza has been selected for the female lead and that the formalities of her contract have been completed, TOB News reported. However, director Himel Ashraf and producer Arshad Adnan have yet to confirm the casting publicly, and the production company, Versatile Media, is reportedly planning to introduce Shakib's new co-star at a special event. Shooting is reportedly set to begin in the first week of January 2027, aiming for an Eid-ul-Azha 2027 release.

Kinza's career so far

Kinza began acting in 2014 and gained recognition through television dramas including Ishq Tamasha, in which she played Rushna, as well as Gul-o-Gulzar, Mohlat, Dil Awaiz, Hook and Mere Ban Jao, plus the telefilm Rooposh. She has also worked in films including Kattar Karachi and Shiroz. Until Versatile Media confirms the casting, the ‘Mohabbat’ role should be treated as reported rather than settled.

articles.title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Agree to Expand TV, Entertainment and Digital Media Ties
articles.description: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to expand cooperation in television, entertainment and digital media, with plans to introduce Pakistani dramas to Saudi audiences and develop joint productions.
articles.sources: Arab News Pakistan, Radio Pakistan, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to expand cooperation in television, entertainment and digital media, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday, as the longtime allies look to deepen cultural exchanges alongside their close defence and economic ties, Arab News Pakistan reported on November 3.

What was agreed

Tarar announced the understanding after meeting Saudi Arabia's new ambassador, Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, in Islamabad. He proposed introducing Pakistani television dramas to Saudi audiences and exchanging delegations of writers, musicians, artists, journalists and digital content creators, according to state broadcaster Radio Pakistan. The minister also called for closer cooperation on fact-checking and combating misinformation, proposing a joint working group of officials and technical experts.

A longer history

The discussions build on previous plans: in 2020, Pakistan announced plans to export television dramas to Saudi Arabia, with Dhoop Kinare, Tanhaiyan and Aahat selected for dubbing, and in February 2025, Tarar and his Saudi counterpart Salman Al-Dossary agreed in Riyadh to establish a joint committee for producing films, songs and documentaries. 'I hope our dramas, art and artists will bring the people of both countries even closer,' Tarar said in a post on social media.

articles.title: World Culture Festival Karachi Screens 'Wakhri' on Its Fourth Day of Theatre, Film and Music
articles.description: The 3rd World Culture Festival Karachi screened Pakistani feature film 'Wakhri' on its fourth day, followed by a Q&A with director Eram Parveen Bilal, as the 25-day festival runs through November 22.
articles.body:
The 3rd World Culture Festival Karachi 2026 reached its fourth day with a dynamic array of international masterclasses, film screenings, theatrical productions and global music and dance showcases at the Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi, Business Cafe reported.

The 'Wakhri' screening

The festival hosted a well-attended screening of the acclaimed Pakistani feature film 'Wakhri', followed by an interactive Q&A session featuring director Eram Parveen Bilal via video link alongside producer Abid Merchant, who engaged with the audience on the film's production and thematic scope. Uruguayan theatre troupe Grieta Teatro also presented 'Chicha', a 45-minute solo physical theatre and clowning performance by artist Betina Andarina, exploring memory and human emotion.

The festival at a glance

The 25-day World Culture Festival Karachi brings together over 1,000 international artists from 150-plus countries alongside 500 Pakistani performers, with daily programming across theatre, music, dance and visual arts. The festival runs through November 22 at the Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi, with public access available via complimentary registration.

articles.title: PTV to Revive Drama and Film Academy With Pakistan's First Local Colour Grading Training
articles.description: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar directed a strategy to revive the PTV Drama and Film Academy as a modern training institution, announcing Pakistan's first local advanced colour grading programme on Monday.
articles.sources: Aaj English TV, ARY News, The Thursday Times, CW Pakistan, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy as a modern training institution, Aaj English TV reported on November 2.

What the revival promises

Chairing a high-level meeting to review plans for the academy's revival and the revamping of PTV Home, Tarar said the institution would equip young people with professional skills in filmmaking, drama production and digital content creation through specialised training programmes, modern technical facilities and practical, industry-oriented models, working with the private sector and universities. He said Pakistan was launching, for the first time, an advanced training programme in colour grading — the post-production adjustment of colour and tone — adding that professionals previously had to travel abroad to learn it.

What is not yet announced

Tarar called the initiative 'game-changing' for Pakistan's creative industry and said young people's creative projects would be encouraged for broadcast on PTV News, PTV Home and other PTV platforms. The reports checked did not give a start date, fees, budget, private-sector partner names or student intake numbers, so those details have yet to be announced. The revival is part of the government's stated commitment to promoting the media and creative industries, the minister said.

articles.title: Ali Zafar's Bostan Khan Look for 'Gangs of Khorasan' Leaves Fans Curious
articles.description: Ali Zafar has revealed a rugged new look — thick moustache, glasses and a transformed appearance — for his character Bostan Khan in the upcoming project 'Gangs of Khorasan,' sparking debate over hero or villain.
articles.sources: GTV News HD, 24 News HD, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistani singer and actor Ali Zafar has surprised fans by revealing his new look for his upcoming project 'Gangs of Khorasan,' where he will play a character named Bostan Khan, GTV News reported on November 2.

The reveal

Zafar shared a glimpse of the character on social media, sporting a thick moustache, glasses and a rugged look — a complete departure from his usual appearance. Fans were left curious about the role, with the central question being whether Bostan Khan will be portrayed as a hero or a villain. Details about the character remain under wraps, GTV noted.

Why fans are watching

The transformation has driven the conversation precisely because so little else is known: no release date, plot synopsis or full cast details were given in the reports checked. Viewers will now wait to see how Zafar brings the mysterious role to life in 'Gangs of Khorasan.' The buzz also fits a wider moment for Pakistani screen talent crossing borders in attention — Indian actor Shoaib Ibrahim praised Pakistani drama 'Dar-e-Nijaat' on November 2, saying he and wife Dipika Kakar regularly watch the show.

articles.title: 'Hum Bhi Jee Lain' Takes On Parental Expectations Pushing Children Into Unwanted Careers
articles.description: The Express Entertainment drama Hum Bhi Jee Lain explores a young man's dilemma when his family's expectations push him towards accountancy while his own ambitions are creative, actor Sharoze Sabzwari told The Express Tribune.
articles.body:
In many Pakistani households, a child's future is often decided long before they are old enough to understand what they actually want to become — and that conflict is at the heart of the Express Entertainment drama Hum Bhi Jee Lain, The Express Tribune reported on November 1.

A writer pushed towards accountancy

Actor Sharoze Sabzwari plays Arsal, a young man with a writer's imagination who is being pushed towards accountancy. Arsal has lost both his parents, leaving his elder sister, played by Faiza Hassan, responsible for raising him and deciding his future. Sabzwari told The Express Tribune the story immediately appealed to him because of the contradiction at the heart of his character: a creative young man caught between his family's expectations and his own ambitions.

Art, and the business of art

While the drama explores the freedom to choose one's own path, Sabzwari also spoke about the challenges of pursuing creative ambitions in Pakistan's entertainment industry. As he put it, art is also a business, and production houses are there to make money at the end of the day — a tension the drama sets against its central question of who gets to decide a young person's future.

articles.title: Sheheryar Munawar Announces New 'Dar-e-Nijaat' OST After Fans Kept Asking for It
articles.description: Actor Sheheryar Munawar has announced a new OST for the drama Dar-e-Nijaat after repeated fan requests, sung by Naveed Nashad and Sehar Gull Khan.
articles.body:
Pakistani actor Sheheryar Munawar has announced the release of a new OST for the drama Dar-e-Nijaat after fans repeatedly requested the song, 24NewsHD reported on November 1.

Who made the new track

The new track is sung by Naveed Nashad and Sehar Gull Khan, with lyrics written by Qamar Nashad and music composed by Naveed Nashad. The latest OST has also sparked comparisons with the drama's original soundtrack, 'Hijr-e-Muhabbat', according to the report.

The drama behind the song

Dar-e-Nijaat is written by Umera Ahmed and directed by Saqib Khan, and airs on ARY Digital. The drama follows the lives of Abu Bakar, Zaryab and Zamil, and has attracted considerable interest from viewers — interest that, in this case, turned into repeated requests for a new song, and now a new OST.

articles.title: 'Ghost School' Opens in Pakistani Cinemas After a Long Censor Battle in Sindh
articles.description: Seemab Gul's festival favourite Ghost School opened in Pakistani cinemas on October 30, after the Sindh censor board's earlier ban and a High Court order for a fresh decision.
articles.body:
Ghost School, the first feature from British-Pakistani filmmaker Seemab Gul, opened in Pakistani cinemas on Friday, October 30, 2026, after a journey home that took in the Toronto International Film Festival, more than a dozen festivals and a best director award in London — and a ban in the province where it was shot.

A film about a school, not a horror story

Despite the title and talk of a jinn, Ghost School is a drama about a 10-year-old girl trying to get her village school reopened, with only a touch of the supernatural. Gul financed the film herself and is paying for its distribution. It is a cinema release, not a drama serial, and no streaming deal has been announced; outside Pakistan it has been showing in German cinemas since September and continues to play at festivals.

The Sindh question

In August, the censor board in Sindh — the province where the film was shot and where its story is set — declared it unfit, but the Sindh High Court ordered the board on October 19 to take a fresh decision within 10 days. At the time of writing, no new Sindh certificate had been reported, while the federal censor board and Punjab's board both cleared the film without cuts. Screenings in Sindh therefore remain dependent on that fresh decision, even as the film opens in Punjab.

articles.title: Faysal Quraishi and Hareem Farooq Decry Alleged 'Smear Campaign' Against 'Mango Jutt'
articles.description: Actors Faysal Quraishi and Hareem Farooq have raised concerns about alleged paid negative publicity targeting their Punjabi-language film Mango Jutt, warning it could hurt Pakistan's struggling cinema industry.
articles.body:
Actors Faysal Quraishi and Hareem Farooq have raised concerns over alleged paid negative publicity targeting their Punjabi-language film Mango Jutt, arguing that coordinated online narratives could hurt not only an individual production but also Pakistan's already struggling cinema industry, The Express Tribune reported on October 29.

Reviews before watching, actors allege

Quraishi addressed the issue in an Instagram video, questioning the practice of publishing negative reviews without watching a film and warning that paid propaganda could undermine the industry's efforts to bring audiences back to cinemas. He noted that many serious film critics wait two to three days, for Friday, Saturday and Sunday to pass, before writing a review. Farooq, who produced and stars in the film, shared screenshots on Instagram that appeared to raise questions about whether some negative posts about the film had been paid for.

Showtimes under pressure

In a separate Instagram post, Farooq highlighted reports that several cinemas had dropped the film, while others had reduced its showtimes or moved screenings away from prime-time slots. For a small industry fighting to rebuild cinema-going, the actors argue, the stakes of an online pile-on go beyond one film's box office — a point that has reignited debate about how films are reviewed and promoted in Pakistan.

articles.title: World Culture Festival 2026 Opens in Karachi With 150 Countries Taking Part
articles.description: The third edition of the World Culture Festival, organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi, formally opens on October 30, 2026, running for 25 days with artists from 150 countries and more than 80 films on show.
articles.body:
The third edition of the World Culture Festival (WCF 2026), organised by the Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi, aims to be all inclusive and pluralistic, council president Ahmed Shah said at a press conference on Thursday evening marking the soft launch of the event. The festival formally starts on Friday, October 30, with the first batch of international artists already arriving in Karachi.

Scale of this year's festival

This year, more than 80 movies, selected out of 6,000 entries from all over the globe, will be screened during the event. Among those who will put their talent on display are Grammy-winning musicians and Oscar-nominated artists. In 2025 the festival spanned 39 days with participation from 140 countries; this time the event will run for 25 days with 150 countries taking part.

Culture as a bridge

Shah said the world is faced with all kinds of challenges as conflicts between countries take place, and that the festival tries to bridge the world through the power of culture and art, because during the event artists from countries such as America, Russia, Palestine and Iran will be seen in action. Sindh Culture Minister Syed Zulfiqar Ali Shah also addressed the press conference, and the evening was to be followed by a qawwali performance by Hamza Akram.

What audiences can expect

With film screenings, music, theatre and performances from 150 countries packed into 25 days, the festival is positioning Karachi as a meeting point for global culture. The Arts Council's festival has grown into one of the city's flagship cultural events, drawing international performers alongside local talent.

Programme details and schedules are expected to be announced by the Arts Council as the festival gets under way.

articles.title: Punjab Plans Stricter Laws for Theatre and Stage Dramas, Replacing 1876 Act
articles.description: The Punjab government has proposed a new Dramatic and Theatrical Performances Bill 2026 to replace the nearly 150-year-old Dramatic Performances Act 1876, with licences, script approvals and fines for violations.
articles.body:
The Punjab government has decided to introduce stricter regulations for stage dramas and theatre performances across the province, proposing a comprehensive legal framework to monitor and regulate theatrical activities, according to Dunya News. The proposed Punjab Dramatic and Theatrical Performances Bill 2026 has surfaced and was presented during the ongoing session before being referred to the relevant committee for consideration.

What the proposed law would require

The proposed legislation aims to repeal the nearly 150-year-old Dramatic Performances Act 1876 and replace it with a modern regulatory and administrative system. Under the proposed law, obtaining a licence from the relevant secretary will be mandatory for staging dramas or theatrical performances at any public venue in Punjab. The proposed licence fee is Rs25,000, while scripts will require prior approval at a proposed fee of Rs35,000. Script Review Committees will be established to examine theatrical scripts and will be notified by the Secretary of the Information and Culture Department.

Restrictions and penalties

The proposed law seeks to prohibit performances deemed obscene, immoral, insulting or objectionable, as well as those that hurt religious sentiments. Under the proposed legislation, violations could carry a punishment of up to six months' imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs1 million.

What happens next

Once approved and enforced, the bill would replace the Dramatic Performances Act 1876, introducing a significantly stricter regulatory framework for theatre and stage productions across Punjab. Because the bill has only been presented and referred to committee so far, its final shape — including the fees and penalties — could still change during the legislative process, and theatre practitioners will be watching the committee stage closely.

The proposal marks one of the most significant overhauls of Punjab's theatre regulation in nearly a century and a half.

articles.title: Faran Tahir Returns to Marvel as Raza in Vision Quest After 18 Years
articles.description: Pakistani-American actor Faran Tahir has reprised his Iron Man villain Raza in episode six of Marvel's Vision Quest, 18 years after his 2008 debut.
articles.body:
Pakistani-American actor Faran Tahir is making headlines once again as he returns to the Marvel universe after 18 years, reprising his role as the villain Raza in the sixth episode of Marvel Studios' series Vision Quest, according to reports published on October 29, 2026.

From Iron Man to Vision Quest

Tahir originally portrayed Raza, the ruthless antagonist who kidnapped Tony Stark, in the blockbuster film Iron Man in 2008. Nearly two decades later, he is back in the same role, sporting a noticeably different look and appearance while bringing the character back to the screen.

What happens in the episode

In the latest episode, Tahir is seen alongside a group of armed associates as they attempt to capture Vision, adding another layer of suspense to the unfolding storyline. The return has been welcomed by fans as a nostalgic callback to the early days of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Why it matters for Pakistani entertainment

His return to the Marvel universe is more than just a nostalgic moment for fans; it is also a proud milestone for Pakistan's entertainment industry. As a Pakistani-origin actor continuing to make his mark on the international stage, Tahir represents the growing presence and talent of Pakistani artists in global cinema.

For audiences who first met Raza in 2008, the comeback closes an 18-year circle, and it underlines how long careers in franchise storytelling can run.

articles.title: Ramayana Buzz Reaches Karachi as Fans Display Film Poster at Temple
articles.description: A circulating video reportedly shows members of Karachi's Hindu community celebrating Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, putting up its poster at a temple ahead of the film's release.
articles.body:
Excitement around Nitesh Tiwari's upcoming film Ramayana has reportedly travelled beyond India's borders, with a video circulating on social media showing members of the Hindu community in Karachi celebrating the film and displaying its poster at a temple, according to reports published on October 29, 2026.

What the circulating video reportedly shows

According to the circulating account, a local YouTuber visited members of Karachi's Hindu community and recorded their reactions to the upcoming film. The video reportedly shows people putting up a Ramayana poster at a temple, beating drums, singing devotional songs and expressing their excitement about the big-screen adaptation. Several participants are said to have conveyed their best wishes to the actors and director, while some expressed hopes that the film would receive recognition at the Oscars. The original footage and its location have not yet been independently verified, so the celebration is described here as reported rather than confirmed.

The film behind the buzz

Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, alongside Sunny Deol and Ravi Dubey, among others. A premiere of Ramayana Part 1 was reported to have been held in Los Angeles on October 27, 2026, with early reviews from the screening described as quite positive. The film is reported to be scheduled for release on November 5, with a second part expected the following Diwali.

Why the Karachi reaction caught attention

The reported celebration drew attention because it showed enthusiasm for an Indian epic adaptation among a community in Pakistan, blending film hype with religious devotion to Lord Rama. Participants in the video were reported to have said they would watch the film and wished the cast success, with one temple priest extending best wishes on behalf of Pakistani Hindus.

Whether or not the film releases in Pakistan itself remains a separate question, and the reports note that some participants appealed for a local release.

articles.title: Humayun Saeed Calls for Pakistan's Own OTT Platform to Take Dramas Global
articles.description: Actor and producer Humayun Saeed says a local streaming platform could help Pakistani dramas reach international audiences.
articles.body:
Actor and producer Humayun Saeed has called for Pakistan to build its own over-the-top (OTT) streaming platform, arguing that a local service could help Pakistani dramas reach international audiences. He added that international productions communicated schedules clearly, while Pakistan's entertainment industry still had room to improve its organisation.

'I do not see myself as a star'

Despite his success, Saeed said he did not consider himself a star and viewed acting as his profession. "I do not see myself as a star. This is just my work. You are not a star for doing it," he said, naming Fahad Mustafa and Fawad Khan as examples of stars. He said he preferred to work in his own way, enjoyed producing projects and maintained a small social circle.

His recent projects include the 2025 romantic comedy Love Guru, directed by Nadeem Baig and co-starring Mahira Khan, and the television drama Main Manto Nahi Hoon, which also aired in 2025. He has also been associated with the Jawani Phir Nahi Ani franchise, with Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 3 reportedly in development. A homegrown platform, his argument runs, would give that kind of work a direct route to viewers abroad, without waiting for foreign services to pick it up.

articles.title: Dananeer Mubeen Teases 'Bullet Speed' Twists Ahead in 'Hurmat'
articles.description: Actress Dananeer Mubeen has hinted at a fast-paced story ahead in 'Hurmat', saying every character must face the consequences of their actions.
articles.body:
Pakistani actress Dananeer Mubeen has sparked curiosity among 'Hurmat' fans after sharing behind-the-scenes pictures and clips from the drama set, teasing more drama ahead. Reacting to the last two episodes, which she described as "HEAVY," the actress hinted at a fast-paced story to come.

Grey characters, fast consequences

Taking to Instagram, Dananeer shared a carousel of behind-the-scenes moments with the playful caption, "Um.... Hurmat? Whatcha doin' up there?" She explained that the lighter content came after two emotionally intense episodes, adding: "The pendulum must swing to an extreme, it's the universe's way. All actions have repercussions." Her words suggest that the characters' decisions may have significant consequences as the story progresses.

Dananeer also highlighted the complexity of the characters, saying: "All characters are grey. There's no such thing as black and white humans. We're all a spectrum of colors." Encouraging viewers to stay patient, she described the upcoming journey as "bullet speed," though she did not reveal any specific twists or plot details. She closed by thanking fans for their support, writing "Hurmat... ka allah hee hafiz haai," and stressing that the love she receives is genuine: "Not paid, not bought. Just genuine love and appreciation."

articles.title: 'Ghost School' Opens in Pakistan Cinemas on October 30 After Censor Court Fight
articles.description: Seemab Gul's festival favourite 'Ghost School', about a young girl fighting to reopen her village school, opens in Pakistani cinemas on October 30 after a court battle over Sindh's refusal to certify it.
articles.body:
Ghost School, the award-winning Pakistani film by British-Pakistani filmmaker Seemab Gul, will release in cinemas across Pakistan on Friday, October 30, 2026. The film is Gul's first feature; she also wrote and produced it. No streaming deal has been announced, with the film opening as a cinema release.

Despite its title and talk of a jinn, Ghost School is not a horror film. It is a drama about a young girl trying to get her school reopened, with only a touch of the supernatural. Nazualiya Arsalan plays Rabia, the young lead, while Samina Seher plays her mother.

What is a 'ghost school'?

In Pakistan, a ghost school is a government school that exists on paper, with a building, a budget and sometimes salaried staff, but which does not actually teach any children. The film uses that reality as the backdrop for Rabia's fight to restore schooling in her village after the school is shut over rumours of a jinn.

The Sindh censor battle

The film's road to release ran through the courts in Sindh. The provincial censor board first called the film not suitable for public exhibition, then demanded eight cuts. The Sindh High Court overturned all but one of those cuts on October 19, and screenings in Sindh now depend on a fresh decision by the provincial censor board following the court's order.

For Pakistani cinema, Ghost School arrives as another example of a film that made its name abroad first: like Hanging by a Wire, Pakistan's Oscar entry this awards cycle, it built its reputation on the festival circuit before reaching home audiences. Its October 30 opening will test whether a small, story-driven film can find a mainstream cinema audience.

The October 30 release also gives audiences a chance to judge the film on its own terms after weeks of coverage focused on the certification dispute. Festival favourites often struggle to convert critical attention into cinema admissions, and Ghost School's opening weekend will show whether word of mouth around its story of a girl fighting for her village school can carry it beyond the headlines.

articles.title: Pakistani Dramas to Watch in October 2026: 'Mitti De Baway' Leads the Month
articles.description: October 2026 brings a fresh wave of Pakistani dramas, led by Mahira Khan and Wahaj Ali's new Green Entertainment serial 'Mitti De Baway', alongside a mystery thriller, a cybercrime story and a gentle romance.
articles.body:
October 2026 has brought a fresh roundup of Pakistani dramas for viewers settling into the autumn season, with new arrivals and longer-running titles sharing the weekly schedule. The month's freshest new entry is Mitti De Baway, positioned as the new arrival going into October, with Mahira Khan and Wahaj Ali leading the cast on Green Entertainment in a Wednesday and Thursday 8:00 PM slot.

For viewers who want something lighter, the roundup points to Dekh Zara Pyaar Se, described as a gentler romance-driven watch compared with the heavier social dramas and mystery titles on the list. The serial stars Yumna Zaidi and Hamza Sohail, with Saima Akram Chaudhry credited as writer.

Thrills, cybercrime and family secrets

For a suspense-first pick, the roundup tags Muamma as its mystery-thriller option, anchored by Saba Qamar and Usman Mukhtar on Hum TV. The cybercrime and digital privacy angle belongs to Aik Aur Pakeezah on Geo Entertainment, with Sehar Khan named as the lead, reflecting how online safety and privacy have become mainstream drama territory.

Family drama is represented by Maa, a Green Entertainment serial in which Raaha, played by Aina Asif, slowly uncovers the reality of her birth and family story. The roundup is presented as unranked, ordered for practical viewing rather than scored by quality, moving from the newest-highlighted entry to longer-running titles.

What to pick

The month's slate covers the main bases of Pakistani television: a star-led new serial in Mitti De Baway, a soft romance in Dekh Zara Pyaar Se, a mystery in Muamma, a contemporary issue drama in Aik Aur Pakeezah, and a family story in Maa. Viewers looking for one new commitment this month will find the strongest case in the Mahira Khan-Wahaj Ali pairing, while those who prefer suspense or social themes have ready alternatives in the same weekly rotation.

articles.title: Pakistani Film 'Wakhri' Selected for UK's South Asian Film Season
articles.description: Pakistani film 'Wakhri', inspired by the story of social media personality Qandeel Baloch, has been selected for Channel 4 and Film4's South Asian Film Season 2026 in the UK.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, October 8, 2026; The AZB, October 8, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistani film 'Wakhri', inspired by the tragic story of social media personality Qandeel Baloch, has been selected for Channel 4 and Film4's South Asian Film Season 2026 in the UK, where it will be showcased alongside a selection of contemporary films from across South Asia. Directed by Iram Parveen Bilal, the film follows Noor Malik, a widowed schoolteacher who becomes an overnight social media sensation after sharing her unfiltered views about life as a woman in modern-day Pakistan.

A story beyond one person

Although the film draws inspiration from Qandeel Baloch's story, its themes extend beyond one individual or country. 'Wakhri' explores questions surrounding women's voices, social expectations, gender inequality, online identity and the pressures that come with sudden visibility on social media. That broader framing is central to the film's appeal: Noor's journey from a classroom to a phone screen, and from private frustration to public scrutiny, mirrors experiences familiar to many women navigating online spaces in South Asia and beyond.

A festival journey to a UK broadcaster

The film previously travelled to several international film festivals, including the Red Sea International Film Festival, Locarno, Cannes and Busan, before its selection for the UK season. This year's South Asian Film Season features nine films from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, spanning drama, thriller and social realism and exploring themes including class, racial, political and gender divides. The season was curated by Indian cinema expert and longtime season consultant Nasreen Munni Kabir. 'Wakhri' was scheduled for its UK broadcast on October 5, followed by online availability, according to reports.

Producer calls it a major validation

Speaking to The Express Tribune, 'Wakhri' producer Abid Merchant described the film's inclusion in the season as an important recognition. He called it a huge validation, saying the film is about a widowed teacher who raises her voice on social media, and that while it is inspired by a tragic story, its message is universal. He added that the film's journey from international film festivals to a major UK broadcaster represented an important milestone for the project.

Why the selection matters

For Pakistani cinema, selection for a curated UK season on a major broadcaster is a meaningful marker of reach. Festival acclaim does not always translate into audiences, but a broadcast slot puts the film in front of viewers who might never attend a film festival. For 'Wakhri', whose subject is the cost of speaking out, that wider audience is part of the point: a story about a woman finding her voice online now gets to find its own audience on television and streaming, far beyond the festival circuit where it began.

articles.title: World Theatre Comes to Lahore as Punjab MAAS Festival Runs to October 28
articles.description: The Lahore Arts Council Alhamra is hosting the Third Punjab MAAS International Theatre Festival 2026 from October 23 to 28, bringing theatre artists from Pakistan and five other countries to Lahore.
articles.sources: Daily Business News, October 2026; MAAS Foundation; Lahore Arts Council Alhamra.
articles.body:
The Lahore Arts Council Alhamra is hosting the Third Punjab MAAS International Theatre Festival 2026 from October 23 to 28, bringing together theatre artists from Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Indonesia, Norway and France to showcase diverse theatrical traditions and promote cultural exchange. The six-day festival features local and international performances, creative workshops and panel discussions exploring artistic freedom, digital culture, social transformation and the role of theatre in engaging younger generations.

A meeting point for world theatre

The MAAS Foundation, a founding member of ASSITEJ Pakistan, and Alhamra describe the festival as a celebration bringing theatre, cultures, languages and people together on one stage. Organisers say that this year Lahore becomes a meeting point for theatre artists from Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Norway and France, bringing diverse stories, artistic traditions and powerful performances to Pakistani audiences. The programme includes performances for children and adults, theatre workshops for children and teenagers, and panel discussions focusing on inclusive theatre and productions for young audiences. From different corners of the world, the organisers say, artists are coming together with one shared belief: theatre has no borders.

Highlights of the programme

The international programme began on October 24 with the University of the Punjab's production of 'Ak Boota Ambi Da', followed by 'Gangster Hunting with Daisy Detective' by Norway's ERLER Teater Kompani. On October 25, a French theatre group presented 'Zig Zag', alongside a panel discussion examining the evolving relevance of theatre in an age dominated by social media. Kazakhstan's Ilyas Omarov Kostanay Regional Kazakh Drama Theatre was scheduled to stage 'Sholpan's Sin' on October 26, while a separate discussion focused on the importance of inclusive and accessible theatre. The festival runs until October 28, giving Lahore audiences a full week of international work.

Why a theatre festival matters now

In an age of short videos and streaming, a live theatre festival makes a different case for attention: a shared room, a live performance and an audience reacting together. The festival's panels on digital culture and artistic freedom speak directly to that tension, asking what live performance can do that a screen cannot. For young audiences, the workshops for children and teenagers are perhaps the most important part of the programme, offering a first taste of making theatre rather than only watching it.

Lahore as a cultural stage

For Lahore, a city with a deep theatre tradition, hosting artists from Central Asia, Europe and South East Asia reinforces its role as a cultural meeting point. The MAAS festival does not just import performances; it creates conversations between Pakistani artists and their international counterparts, conversations that can lead to future collaborations long after the final curtain on October 28. For audiences still deciding whether to attend, the remaining days offer a rare chance to see world theatre without leaving the city.

articles.title: 'Mango Jutt' Punjabi Action-Comedy Hits Cinemas
articles.description: Hareem Farooq produces and stars in Abu Aleeha's Punjabi action-comedy, which premiered in Lahore on October 15 and released nationwide on October 16.
articles.sources: GTV News; The Express Tribune, October 11, 2026; 24 News HD.
articles.body:
Pakistani actress and producer Hareem Farooq's latest Punjabi action-comedy film, Mango Jutt, has been released nationwide on October 16, 2026, after a star-studded premiere in Lahore. The film's grand premiere took place at CineStar in Township, Lahore, on October 15, where several celebrities, media representatives, social media influencers and other guests gathered to celebrate the release.

A Punjabi story for all of Pakistan

Produced by Hareem Farooq under the banner of Hameem Productions, Mango Jutt is a Punjabi action comedy that brings together action, humour, romance and Punjabi cultural elements. Hareem, who also plays the lead role, attended the premiere alongside the film's cast and crew. The movie stars Faysal Quraishi, Shamoon Abbasi, Qaiser Piya and comedy actor Iftikhar Thakur, among others, with Ayesha Jahanzeb and Honey Albela also in supporting roles. Abu Aleeha has written and directed the film. Speaking to The Express Tribune at the film's music launch in Karachi, Farooq said the project had been a challenging but rewarding experience, adding that bringing it to the screen was a success in itself. "My message is that people should watch this film with an open heart. It is for all of Pakistan. Just because it is a Punjabi film does not mean it is only for Punjab. It is a film for the entire country," she said.

Music, trailer buzz and a starry premiere

Music is another feature of the film, with Ali Mustafa and Ali Allah Ditta directing its original soundtrack. Singers including Falak Shabbir, Zeb Bangash and Jabbar Abbas have contributed to the music. The trailer had already drawn attention, with its mix of cops, goons, romance and comedy, and its closing scene — Shamoon Abbasi's antagonist dragging the heroine away as his henchmen hold Jutt down — setting up the film's action payoff. The Lahore premiere drew showbiz personalities including Fawad Khan and Wahaj Ali, whose friendly interaction inside the cinema drew attention from fans. Farooq said audience feedback had been encouraging and expectations had risen as the film's release approached.

What Mango Jutt means for Lollywood

Mango Jutt arrives as part of a growing lineup of Pakistani movies planned for theatrical release this year, and its bet is a distinctive one: that Punjabi-language storytelling, played with colour and confidence, can draw audiences from across the country rather than only from Punjab. Farooq said visiting Karachi for the launch was particularly meaningful because of the affection she had received from the city, and that completing the film had already made the journey worthwhile. Whether the film becomes a box-office hit will be decided by audiences in the weeks ahead — but as a statement of intent for regional-language cinema, Mango Jutt is already hard to ignore.

articles.title: Dar-e-Nijaat Tops 2026 TV Ratings at 16.3 TRP
articles.description: The ARY Digital drama starring Durefishan Saleem and Sheheryar Munawar hit 16.3 TRPs in its latest promotional update — with one honest caveat about the comparison figure.
articles.sources: The Siasat Daily, October 2026; ARY Digital.
articles.body:
Pakistani television's ratings race has a fresh talking point, and this time, Durefishan Saleem and Sheheryar Munawar are in the spotlight. Their ongoing drama, Dar-e-Nijaat, has recorded an impressive figure in its latest promotional update, giving its leading man a reason to celebrate. A ratings poster shared on Sheheryar's Instagram Story puts the drama at 16.3 TRPs, with the accompanying text describing it as the highest rating achieved by any drama in 2026.

The drama behind the number

Written by Umera Ahmed and directed by Saqib Khan, Dar-e-Nijaat brings together Durefishan and Sheheryar in a story centred on heartbreak, destiny and redemption. Its ensemble also includes Nameer Nawaz Khan, Sahar Hashmi, Romaisa Khan, Sania Saeed and Saba Hamid. The drama had already drawn attention for Sheheryar's portrayal of Abu Bakar: actress Zara Noor Abbas previously praised his Quranic recitation in a scene and also appreciated Romaisa Khan's performance as Hamna. The actor reshared the ratings announcement with "Alhumdulillah" and a folded-hands emoji, and the update prompted social media comparisons with Zanjeerain, with the circulating post claiming that Dar-e-Nijaat has moved ahead.

An honest caveat about the comparison

Here, honesty matters more than hype. The promotional image does not provide Zanjeerain's corresponding figure, nor does it specify the audience category and measurement period for the comparison. So while the 16.3 TRP figure itself comes from the drama's own promotional poster, shared by its lead actor, the claim that it "overtakes" Zanjeerain rests on the promotional post alone — the source did not publish the rival figure that would let readers check the comparison for themselves. Readers should treat the top-spot claim as a promotional claim, not an independently verified ratings ranking, until a ratings agency figure for both dramas over the same period is published.

Where and when to watch

Dar-e-Nijaat airs on ARY Digital every Friday and Saturday at 8 pm Pakistan time, with episodes also available to stream through the ARY Plus app. With the latest ratings announcement adding to the interest around the show, the question now is whether it can keep that momentum going in the coming weeks. On the evidence of its social media buzz — and a lead pair whose chemistry has become the show's calling card — the audience, at least, seems in no hurry to switch off. That distinction — between a promotional poster figure and an independently audited ranking — is worth keeping in mind whenever a drama's ratings are celebrated online, since posters rarely publish the methodology behind the headline number.

articles.title: Ali Zafar to Make His Pakistani TV Drama Debut in a New Crime Series
articles.description: The singer-actor headlines a high-budget crime and mafia-themed series directed by Anas Ali, with Humaima Malik, Feroze Khan and Sonya Hussyn in the ensemble.
articles.body:
Pakistani singer and actor Ali Zafar is set to make his acting comeback with an upcoming crime series, marking a major new chapter in his career on screen. Known for his musical talent, distinctive style and versatile performances, Ali Zafar has enjoyed success in Bollywood as well as earned considerable appreciation in Pakistani cinema — and now, after years of fans urging him toward television, he is finally coming to the small screen on home turf.

A debut years in the making

According to reports, the big-budget crime series will be directed by Anas Ali and feature a star-studded cast, including Humaima Malik, Feroze Khan and Sonya Hussyn in key roles. The project is described as a high-budget, mafia-themed crime story. Fans have long awaited Ali Zafar's return to small-screen drama: he had previously agreed to be part of Lahu, a drama featuring Sajal Aly and Bilal Abbas Khan, before eventually stepping away from the project. His last television appearance was in the serial College Jeans, making this new series his first major small-screen lead in years — and, as several reports describe it, his debut in a Pakistani web or television series in the modern sense.

The ensemble around him

Humaima Malik joins him as a lead, returning to the screen after a period of selective television appearances. She broke through in Shoaib Mansoor's Bol and later played the fierce Daro in the record-breaking The Legend of Maula Jatt, before returning strongly in Jindo. Feroze Khan and Sonya Hussyn round out the key cast, both well known to drama audiences through memorable television performances across a wide variety of roles. Putting all four names together in a crime-themed story is a combination that few viewers saw coming, and it is precisely why the announcement has caught fire online.

What is still unknown

The makers have yet to announce the storyline, streaming platform or release date, and the series remains untitled in published reports. What is known is the genre, the director and the scale of ambition: a large-scale production aiming at high-quality, big-budget storytelling in local television. For Pakistani viewers, the project matters beyond one star's comeback — it reunites talented actors who have captivated audiences across music, film and television, and it tests whether a crime saga with this calibre of cast can raise the bar for the whole industry. Until the title and airdate land, fans will have to settle for the announcement itself — which, judging by the reaction, was more than enough.
